name: The Render Shoals

detectability.signature: Roaring gravimetric shear bands in alternating pull; debris impacts register on scopes as continuous static

proximity: Hulls groan under alternating tidal stretch and squeeze every few minutes
Debris swarms deflect small craft off course without warning
contact: Shear bands peel plating from vessels that cross them at the wrong phase
Collision probability with tumbling rock exceeds seventy percent per crossing attempt
prolonged_exposure: Structural fatigue cracks propagate through frames within hours of sustained exposure
Crews suffer stress fractures and chronic motion sickness from cyclic hull flexing

known_incidents: The salvage rig Anvil's Pride broke into three sections during a shear surge with only half her crew recovered
Pirate crews use the shoals' chaos to break pursuit tails, knowing navy captains rarely follow
description: The Render Shoals is a churning belt of shattered rock and shredded hull metal caught between the tidal grips of two dense stellar cores. Shear bands sweep through the field like invisible scythes, alternately stretching and compressing everything in their path. To the eye it is a glittering storm of debris; to gravimetrics it is a howl.

The field orbits its twin foci in tangled loops, and the shear bands realign on a rough nineteen-hour cycle that surveyors have never pinned to a schedule. One crossing may pass uneventfully; the next, same heading, same hour, meets a band that peels armor plating like foil. Veterans call a successful transit 'threading the loom' and refuse to predict one.

The shoals formed eighty million years ago when a wayward gas giant was torn apart during a close binary encounter, and they have been grinding ever since. The Anvil's Pride disaster ended commercial salvage here, though her wreck, and dozens of others, still drift rich with untouched cargo. Rare metals torn from the giant's core concentrate in the calmer eddies.

Insurance boards blacklisted the region, which suits the pirates who shelter there just fine. Prospectors still run the edge currents for core-metal nuggets, and recovery teams occasionally return with intact prizes from deeper water. Every run is a wager against a loom whose pattern no one has ever fully read.
